findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-code credential cannot be removed via removeStoredCredentialById
findings.body: After switching to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), the credential found may now be a federated (user-storage) credential rather than a locally stored one. When all codes are used, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()), but removeStoredCredentialById only removes credentials stored in the Keycloak DB; for a federated credential (id prefixed with the storage provider, or an id generated by the storage) this call silently does nothing. The exhausted credential stays active in the user storage, so the user is forced into the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action on every login while the dead credential remains listed/valid. The removal needs to go through the storage provider's disable/update path, or be skipped for federated credentials.

findings.title: Creating recovery codes in user storage leaves a pre-existing local recovery credential active
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() first tries user.credentialManager().updateCredential(); if the user storage accepts the recovery-codes type it stores the credential there and returns, never removing any previously stored local (Keycloak DB) recovery-code credential for that user. The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential() path replaces the existing credential, so the previous behavior guaranteed a single active credential. With this change a user who already had a local recovery credential and whose storage now supports the type ends up with two simultaneously valid recovery-code credentials (one local, one federated), and the old one is never invalidated. The user-storage branch should also remove any stored local credential of the same type (or the check should be skipped when a local credential exists).

findings.title: User label and generatedAt are not propagated to user storage when creating recovery codes
findings.body: When delegating to the user storage via updateCredential(), the UserCredentialModel carries only the JSON list of raw codes (challengeResponse). The userLabel and generatedAt timestamp that are part of the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel are dropped, so a user storage that wants to persist them cannot (the test provider's stored CredentialModel never has a user label). If the UserCredentialModel cannot carry them, this limitation should at least be documented on the method, since storages implementing CredentialInputUpdater for this type receive an input with no way to reconstruct the full credential.

findings.title: getCredentials() returns a freshly generated credential id on every call and drops the stored one; NPE for unknown user
findings.body: In getCredentials(), the recovery-codes CredentialModel is rebuilt via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...), which generates a new random id each call instead of returning myUser.recoveryCodes with its stored id. Consequently the credential id reported to Keycloak is unstable (changes between calls), so operations like deleting the credential by id via the account REST endpoint (as the existing OTP test does) cannot work for recovery codes, and the stored id set in updateCredential() is effectively unused. Also, getMyUser(user) may return null for an unknown user and myUser.recoveryCodes would throw an NPE instead of returning an empty stream. Additionally, disableCredentialType() does not handle RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE even though supportsCredentialType() advertises it, so disabling recovery codes through the admin REST API silently logs 'unsupported' and leaves the credential in place — none of these paths are covered by the new test.
